findings.summary: This loosens a control, and no recorded decision covers it. The rule 'an answered decision is final' becomes 'an answered decision with no `by` can be superseded'. The event log on this branch has 94 operator-answered events with no `by`, for example DEC-0061, DEC-0068, DEC-0083 and DEC-0123 to DEC-0146. Many are probably real operator rulings recorded while `--by` was optional. `supersede` has no caller-role check (decisions.ts around line 2140), so any session can now close one of those rulings with `cli-decisions supersede DEC-0123 --by DEC-XXXX --reason x`, and the projection will mark it superseded. I checked the log: no existing superseded event changes state under the new fold, so nothing breaks today; the risk is in future use. Narrow the rule to the DEC-0091 shape (no `by`, no rationale, and the chosen option equals `autonomousFallback`), or record a decision that authorizes the wider rule. The same predicate is duplicated in decisions.ts at line 2190 and must stay in sync.

findings.summary: The `resolve` subcommand (`--option` form, around lines 2040-2115) can still write an `operator-answered` event with no `by` and no rationale. Only `answer` now requires `--by` and `--rationale`. So the writer path AC3 targets is closed for `answer` and the TUI pane, but not for `resolve`. Because the projection and supersede changes now let any decision answered with no `by` be superseded, a `resolve` answer given without `--by` can later be closed by any session that runs `supersede`. Nobody untrusted can reach this (the event log is changed only through commits that pass review), so it is a consistency gap, not something an attacker can use. Suggestion: apply the same `--by`/`--rationale` checks to `resolve`.

findings.summary: Loosening the projection rule applies to every past event, not just DEC-0091. Any existing `superseded` event that targets a decision answered with no `by` will now flip that decision from answered to superseded when the log is replayed. Auto-expired answers are safe because the projection defaults `answeredBy` to 'auto-expired'. The other writers in the code (webhook-health, dor-at-import, reconcile, and now the TUI) all set `by`. Worth confirming in the PR body that the current event log has no such superseded-after-answer pair other than DEC-0091.
